sentences.text: Solicitor Daniel Hughes attended the meeting with client Chloe Mason.
The purpose of the meeting was to discuss the council's letter before proceedings and the meeting scheduled for December 1st.
Chloe Mason is the client in this meeting.
Chloe Mason arrived by 42 bus.
Poppy is 14 months old and is walking everywhere.
Alfie attends Little Stars nursery on Bank Street, Monday to Friday, mornings.
Alfie is a fussy eater and only eats pasta and fish fingers.
Alfie sleeps from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.
The council's letter cites concerns about a bruise on Alfie's arm seen by nursery on November 9th and police being called to the house in October.
Chloe told social worker Ms Okoye that Alfie fell off the sofa.
Chloe stated that Jordan slapped Alfie across the face because he wouldn't eat his tea.
The incident where Jordan slapped Alfie occurred on Sunday, November 8th, around 5 o'clock.
The bruise on Alfie's arm came from Jordan grabbing him by the arm and pulling him off a chair.
Chloe was at the sink when she saw the bruise on Alfie's arm.
Jordan told Chloe to say that Alfie fell off the sofa when the social worker Ms Okoye arrived.
The police were called in October after a neighbour rang them following an argument and shouting between Chloe and Jordan.
Jordan is currently at his mother's house this week and will return on Saturday.
Chloe wants her children to stay with her.
Chloe stated that if she leaves Jordan, he says he will take the children, specifically Poppy, because she is his.
Jordan has never taken the children anywhere without Chloe's agreement.
Chloe gave permission for the solicitor to write to Ms Okoye with the information provided during the meeting.
Jordan cannot take the children without going to court, and a court would hear about what happened to Alfie.
Chloe can apply for a non-molestation order to stop Jordan from coming to the house.
Chloe can likely get legal aid for a non-molestation order.
Solicitor advised Chloe to tell social worker Ms Okoye the truth about what happened to Alfie, before the December 1st meeting, to protect Alfie and Chloe.
Solicitor advised that if the children are taken anyway, a mother who tells the truth and acts to keep her child safe is in a stronger position than one who supports her partner's谎
The solicitor will write to Ms Okoye by Thursday, the 26th, with Chloe's account details and send a copy to her.
The solicitor will call Harbridge Women's Aid today to discuss a safety plan for when Jordan returns on Saturday.
The solicitor will prepare a non-molestation application for Chloe.
The next meeting with Chloe will be on Monday, the 30th, to review the non-molestation application and prepare for the December 1st meeting.
